text: I’ll build the standalone geometry contract and its focused node tests, keeping the route explicitly illustrative rather than GPS physics.

Implemented the assigned geometry module and tests.

- [geometry.js]([local-path]) exports the full requested pure ES-module contract, including stable 2D/3D intersection handling and a documented, deterministic 20-second illustrative car route.
- [geometry.test.js]([local-path]) verifies circle and sphere distance constraints, tangencies, disjoint/concentric cases, triple-sphere results, and route continuity and overlay stops.
- Validation passed: `node --test tests/geometry.test.js` — **5 passing, 0 failing**.

The repository’s root `.gitignore` currently ignores these new files through `/*`; they will need `git add -f` when the parent stages the project. Node also emitted a non-blocking module-type warning because the ancestor package has no `"type": "module"`, while correctly executing the ES-module tests.
I’ll add a single-worker browser suite against the running local Vite story, deriving selectors and timing expectations from its public UI before I write assertions.

The suite is in place; the first run was blocked before loading the local app because Playwright’s bundled Chromium executable is absent. I’ll use the installed Edge channel if present, as permitted, then rerun the actual checks.

Implemented the browser regression suite in [playwright.config.js]([local-path]) and [browser.spec.js]([local-path]).

`npx playwright test --workers=1` passes all 7 checks against the local Vite app. The suite covers playback, chapter selection, speed cycling, all 17 chapter seeks with canvas/WebGL error monitoring, keyboard controls and replay, reduced motion, and desktop/mobile layout bounds and overlap checks.

Inspection screenshots are in `test-results/`:

- `autoplay-paused.png`
- `chapter-dialog-selection.png`
- `all-chapters-final.png`
- `layout-1920x1080.png`
- `layout-390x844.png`

Playwright’s bundled Chromium was unavailable, so the config uses the installed Microsoft Edge channel. The project’s root `.gitignore` ignores the new test files through `/*`; stage them with `git add -f` when committing.
